blocks.text: Jehu is commissioned to carry out judgment on Ahab’s house (vv. 1–10), but that commission does not make every later action or method exemplary. The account later presents Jehu as destroying institutional Baal worship while also faulting his continued adherence to Jeroboam’s shrines; Hosea subsequently condemns the bloodshed at Jezreel. The chapter’s prophetic authorization should therefore be read as a specific commission, not as an unqualified approval of everything associated with Jehu’s rule.

The Black Obelisk of Shalmaneser III depicts and captions tribute from Jehu, or from the house identified with Omri: it shows prostration before the Assyrian king, tribute bearers, and listed luxury and royal goods. This provides near-contemporary external evidence of Jehu’s submission to Assyria, a political relationship not reported in 2 Kings 9–10. It does not, however, verify the chapter’s coup narrative or supply an image of the events described here.
